newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to start second board to boost liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to start second board to boost liquidity.

text.p: Sri Lanka will introduce a second board by January 1997 to improve share liquidity on the Colombo Stock Exchange, a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) official said on Wednesday.
The second board should be in place in the first quarter of 1997, said Arittha Wikramanayake, director general of the SEC which regulates the market.
"Listing requirements for second board companies will be less stringent than for those on the main boards, because we want to encourage businesses to get quoted," he said.
The ultimate aim was to help second board companies graduate to the main board and to improve Colombo's woefully inadequate share liquidity, he said.
A second board company (SBC) will have to issue 10 percent of its capital to the public, while a main board company (MBC) has to issue at least 25 percent.
A SBC will need a minimum of 50 shareholders to get listed. An MBC needs at least 300 shareholders, each holding between 300 and 10,000 shares.
The paid-up capital of an SBC will have to be at least five million rupees. It is 75 million rupees for an MBC.
An SBC can publish six-monthly accounts while quarterly reports are mandatory for an MBC.
Second board companies will not need a three-year track record which is essential to be listed on the main board.
"A main board company which falls short of the requirements will be put on notice and relegated to the second board on failure to comply," said Wikramanayake.
